title: Argon Laser: Precision Photocoagulation in Ophthalmology
summary: The Argon laser is a gas-based laser emitting blue-green light, serving as a cornerstone for thermal treatment in retinal and glaucoma conditions. It works by converting light energy into heat to coagulate targeted ocular tissues.

sections.title: Mechanism of Action
content: Step 1: Light emission in the blue-green spectrum.
Step 2: Absorption by ocular chromophores (Melanin and Hemoglobin).
Step 3: Conversion of radiant energy into thermal energy.
Step 4: Protein denaturation and tissue coagulation.

content.explanation: B: Blue-Green wavelengths; G: Gas-medium laser; T: Thermal mechanism (Photocoagulation).

sections.title: Contraindications & Red Flags
content: Opaque Media (e.g., dense cataract or vitreous hemorrhage) preventing beam focus.
Tractional Retinal Detachment involving the macula.
Severe Foveal Ischemia (caution with focal treatment).
Patient inability to maintain fixation during delivery.

sections.title: Treatment Parameters (Example: ALT)
content: Power: Adjusted to achieve 'champagne bubble' reaction
Location: Junction of pigmented and non-pigmented trabecular meshwork

sections.title: Laser Definitions
sections.content: The term LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. The Argon laser specifically uses ionized argon gas as its active medium, requiring high-voltage electricity to achieve population inversion and generate its characteristic coherent beam.
